result.title: A Human-Verified AI Workflow for Annotating Environmental Sound Data
result.summary: Large-scale annotation of environmental sound recordings presents significant challenges under time and resource constraints, particularly when sound categories are imbalanced and only part of a dataset has been labeled. This paper describes the development and evaluation of a human-AI workflow used during annotation of the Kenya Forest Sounds Dataset (KFSD), using a project-stage working collection of 7,531 audio recordings across 21 categories. We investigated zero-shot classification, a feature-based ensemble, and a fine-tuned Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST). The fine-tuned AST achieved 89.36% accuracy, 85.98% precision, 89.24% recall, and 87.58% F1 on held-out test data for binary classification of Person talking. Because this result remained below the predefined 95% threshold for autonomous annotation, model predictions were used as suggestions and subjected to human verification. Of the 5,026 initially unlabeled recordings, 2,337 were routed to a speech-verification queue and 2,689 remained for ordinary manual annotation. The verifier reviewed all 2,337 machine-labeled files and detected zero false positives, yielding 100% verification accuracy. The observed average verification time was approximately 4.2 seconds per file. At an average rate of 35 seconds per file for manual annotation, the hybrid workflow reduced work on the remaining queue from approximately 48.9 to 28.9 person-hours, saving about 20.0 hours (41%). The study documents the model-selection process, provenance-aware file organization, verification procedure, observed errors, practical limitations, and opportunities for extending AI assistance beyond one category.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在肯尼亚森林声音数据集上搭建并评估人工-AI 标注流程：比较零样本分类、特征集成与微调 AST，因精度未达预设自动标注阈值，改以模型预测作为建议交由人工核验，并统计核验耗时与工时节省。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按阈值决定哪些样本需人工核验、并核算核验与纯人工标注成本差异的做法，可能与 LVR 中何时追加证据核查及停止决策的成本权衡形成概念类比，可供核查；但对象是音频分类，缺乏推理状态层面的联系。
